repository_scope.note: Repository list and README reconnaissance for the 50 GitHub-accessible repos, then keyword code searches and source-file checks for relevant projects; NOT a file-by-file audit of every code/data object.

primary_question: Can head orientation and true involucral spines form a guild-dependent joint access barrier affecting effective pollination, seed predation and viable achenes, and is that interaction linked to correlated evolution?

classifications.claim_ceiling: Public-data feasibility/prior-art audit and prospective falsifiable hypothesis only. No evidence of adaptation, coevolution, selection, or direct defence by focal thistle spines.

evidence.boundary: Image projection prominence and image vertical angle, not botanical spine length nor gravity orientation. RV is undirected.
Phyllary posture is not spine morphology, and joint available n=8 is not a credible basis for a phylogenetic dependency test.
Different lower-bound state histories do not exclude indirect, context-dependent correlated selection and do not prove spine coevolution.
Antagonist fitness pressure only. Not spine, head-angle, or interaction effect.
Heterogeneous other floral systems; mechanisms plausibility and route classification only, not thistle angle-spine selection.

evidence.design: 24 plants non-destructive bract-gap proxy, paired feasibility, no angle manipulation
evidence.boundary: Cannot relabel existing 2-arm feasibility pilot as powered/approved 2x2 factorial.
Adaptive camera evidence not independent confirmed visitation, behaviour, or pollen transfer.

comparative_prior_art.finding: Spines selectively deter illegitimate Lepidoptera, no increase in legitimate bee/fly visit probability when removed; 22% lower filled seeds after spine removal.
comparative_prior_art.gap: No head-angle manipulation and not Cirsium

comparative_prior_art.finding: Plant display attracts bumblebee use yet increases pre-dispersal seed predation risk.
comparative_prior_art.gap: No joint orientation x spine experiment

critical_falsifiers: External-ovipositor and legitimate-visitor access rates react similarly to O x S even with verified manipulations
Effects disappear after within-head anthesis stage and reference orientation QC
Enemy entry bypasses involucre via stem/internal developmental route
Final viable-achene effects come only through rain/UV timing or plant-size contrasts
Present interaction has no corroborating genetic/phylogenetic evolutionary dependence
